- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to underpredict (especially in early forecast horizon), so adjust upward by 1–2% for 1–3 day horizons.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts and forecasts continued ascent — correct by reducing forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to pivot — force a mean-reversion correction toward recent 7-day average, especially if true outcome shows divergence.
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — add 3–5% bias to 30d forecast if sentiment > -0.5.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after a spike, model often lags — correct by adding 1–2 days of downward momentum in forecast, especially if sentiment remains negative.
- When sentiment is positive but model forecasts remain flat or declining, increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days to reflect sentiment momentum.
